# OS Compatibility

Where the StackKits lifecycle was tested for the current public release. Every row is projected from
automated lifecycle receipts (install, init, generate, apply, verify, backup, restore) bound to the
exact release; missing evidence is `unverified`, never an implied pass.

- StackKits release: `v0.33.3`
- Last observed: 2026-09-16T21:03:18Z

Grades: `supported` = every lifecycle phase passed on this release; `preview` = install through verify
passed, a later phase did not; `unverified` = no passing receipt for this release.

## Operating systems

The lifecycle runs install each operating system fresh in a KVM/QEMU virtual machine.

| linux | ubuntu | `24.04` | amd64 | **✅ supported** | All lifecycle phases passed | `v0.33.3` |
| linux | debian | `13` | amd64 | **🟡 preview** | Backup phase failed on this release | — |
| linux | debian | `12` | — | **⚪ unverified** | Not covered by the automated lifecycle tests yet | — |

## Hypervisors

StackKits run inside a guest VM on your hypervisor, never on the hypervisor host itself. The grade
covers that rollout end to end: the guest is created on the hypervisor and the StackKit lifecycle
runs inside it.

| Hypervisor | How the guest is created | Grade | Evidence | Last verified |
| --- | --- | :-: | --- | --- |
| Proxmox VE | kombify Techstack or the Proxmox VE API creates an Ubuntu 24.04 guest VM; the StackKit installs inside that guest and is reached from the home network. | **✅ supported** | All lifecycle phases passed | `v0.33.3` |

## Authority boundary

The only writer of this data is the receipt projector (`scripts/compat/project-os-compat.mjs`) through
an auto-PR. Rows never name a server provider, and host diagnostics never create a claim.

Run `stackkit compat` on a target for non-destructive host diagnostics and the published evidence
for its OS and hypervisor.
